newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy to take all measures to meet EMU goal - Ciampi.
newsitem.headline: Italy to take all measures to meet EMU goal - Ciampi.

text.p: Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said on Wednesday that the Italian government would do everything to ensure the ratio between the public deficit and Gross Domestic Product (GDP) in 1997 met the 3.0 percent target required for membership of Europe's planned single currency.

He told a news conference that it was "not the right time" to ask whether a mini-budget would be required early next year to achieve the ratio, but added: "We will take the measures that we think are necessary to meet the objective."

Critics of the centre-left government's budget, which aims to cut the 1997 deficit by 62.5 trillion lire, say it will fail to get Italy into Europe's planned monetary union and that a supplementary budget will be needed to meet the deficit target.
Ciampi also said the new currency, the euro, should be as strong as the German mark when it is introduced in January 1999.
"There is no doubt that our aim is the creation of the single currency, which gives rise to a currency as strong as the deutsche mark," he said.
